text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] DNS error rate spike detected for api.redwood.ai from multiple EU resolvers (Cloudflare/ISP). Anomalous NXDOMAIN and SERVFAILs — start=2026-03-15T09:02:41Z. Paging on-call SRE. :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: I see it. Dashboards showing resolver error rate to eu-west1 up to 12%. Traces: client requests timing out at name resolution step.

alice.nguyen: Confirmed. Route53 health checks for endpoints are green. But authoritative responses vary between resolvers. Some CF POPs are serving stale NS sets (split-horizon-like behavior).

ben.choi: Quick dig from two resolvers shows different outcomes (started 09:03 UTC):
```bash
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai +short
10.200.34.12
$ dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai +short
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai +short
;  (no answer)
$ dig @1.0.0.1 api.redwood.ai +short
; connection timed out.
```

mohit.rao: Impact assessment: hosted API 95th percentile latency in EU up ~400ms (due to retries) and ~4% of requests returning 502/504. Customer reported increased generation failures in EU.

eng-runtime: Noted that geo-routing policy had a recent change yesterday to add a CF-based responder group for faster failover. Possibly CF POPs have a stale zone copy.

cloudflare-bot: Cloudflare ticket #CF-87321 opened; assigned to Network Operations. Initial reply: "seeing divergence in delegated NS across POPs, investigating replication."

support-ops: We have two enterprise customers complaining (sales flagged). Escalate comms?

sre-oncall: Mitigation plan (short-term):
- Route traffic away from CF-backed GeoDNS responders to Route53 canonical mapping for EU (force Route53 responses where possible).
- Reduce TTL for affected records to 30s to accelerate propagation during failover window.
- Add HA fallback: map eu requests to us-west pool for critical customer routes while CF resolves.

alice.nguyen: I'll run the TTL and routing change now. Command to update traffic policy (internal tooling):
```bash
# set geo policy preference to route53-first for EU region (dry-run then apply)
redwoodctl dns set-policy --region eu --preference route53 --ttl 30 --apply
```

ben.choi: Applying dry-run shows expected change; pushing apply. Watching live synthetic checks.

sre-oncall: Apply done at 09:09 UTC. Synthetic probes show resolution consistency improving to 98% within ~60s. Monitoring for regressions.

cloudflare-bot: CF acknowledges many POPs cleared but a few still showing stale NS. They estimate full convergence ~15-20m.

mohit.rao: Handoff: I'm taking the incident for the next shift at 09:20 UTC. Summary for the next on-call:
- Root cause likely replication lag/stale delegations inside a subset of Cloudflare POPs after zone sync + our recent geo-responder addition increased reliance on those POPs.
- Impact: EU resolver lookup errors -> ~4-6% client error rate for hosted API; degraded latency. Some enterprise customers impacted.
- Mitigations in place: route53-first geo policy, TTL=30, temporary routing for critical flows to us-west.
- Open tickets: Cloudflare #CF-87321, internal postmortem thread.

eng-runtime: Logging action items:
- Revert geo-responder rollout until CF confirms stable replication.
- Add a canary step to verify NS consistency across CF POPs before promoting responder.

support-ops: Noted. Drafting a short customer-facing status update to affected accounts now.

alice.nguyen: Can we get a packet-level dump from one of affected CF POPs? CF asked for query samples; I uploaded dig output and synthetic timestamps to ticket.

ben.choi: Observability: Added a resolver-consistency alert and a quick query that compares answers from 6 public resolvers every 30s. Will keep it active for 24h.

cloudflare-bot: CF updated ticket: "partial rollback of zone distribution triggered, propagation continuing. No DNSSEC issues observed."

mohit.rao: Current status @09:25 UTC: error rates down to 1.1% EU-wide, latency trending down. Keeping incident active for monitoring and handoff notes. Next: postmortem to include rollout gating for geo-responder and automated NS-consistency checks.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=sev2, started=4145678901, mitigation="route53-preference + ttl=30 + temporary us-west mapping", responders=[sre-oncall,mohit.rao,alice.nguyen,ben.choi,eng-runtime], tickets=[CF-87321].

sre-oncall: Closing notes: follow up actions assigned, library of DNS runbooks updated with CF replication checklist. If error rate creeps back above 3% in any region, re-open paging. :white_check_mark:

support-ops: I'll keep customers updated and coordinate postmortem distribution.
